userStories.title: API fix follow-up event
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Record an attempt-specific follow-up event when a FIX completes after pushing code, with a reusable typed payload builder and parser.

**Motivation** — Today nothing reviews the head a FIX pushed unless auto-review is on for the repo.

**Approach** — 1. **Trigger: an outbox event recorded in the terminal transaction.** `FleetJobOutcomeRecorder.onTerminal` already runs inside `JobTransitionsService.apply`'s transaction for every terminal job. It gains a first step: for a `FIX` job in `COMPLETED` whose `fixOutcome` is `pushed`, it records one `fleet_fix_follow_up` outbox event. This step comes before the method's existing agent-requester and thread-kind early return, because an agent's FIX gets a follow-up too. The step needs `resultSha` non-null and a feature `prNumberOfReviewFeature` can parse. Without both, nothing is recorded. The outbox relay delivers the event after commit, so no dispatch runs inside the job report transaction. (A dispatch opens its own transaction, and a 409 must not poison the caller's, the `ScheduleTicker` rule.) `FleetJobOutcomeRecorder` keeps its constructor, so no injection site changes.

2. **The event's payload is a snapshot**: `{ jobId, leaseEpoch, projectId, repoId, prNumber, headSha, requestedById, requestedByType, profiles, maxCostUsd }`. `headSha` is the FIX's `resultSha`. `requestedByType` is the record's value, or `'USER'` when the record has none (the column default). `maxCostUsd` is the record's decimal string. `metadata` is `{ projectId, eventId: '<jobId>:<leaseEpoch>:fix-follow-up' }`, so a requeued FIX that pushes again gets its own event.

`apps/api/src/fleet/common/fix-follow-up-events.ts`: `FIX_FOLLOW_UP = 'fleet_fix_follow_up'`, the `FixFollowUpPayload` type (call 2), `buildFixFollowUpPayload(job: FleetJobRecord, prNumber: number, headSha: string): FixFollowUpPayload`, and `parseFixFollowUpPayload(raw: unknown): FixFollowUpPayload | null`. The parser returns `null` when any field is missing or mistyped: `requestedByType` must be `'USER'` or `'AGENT'`, `prNumber` a positive safe integer, `profiles` an array of strings, and `maxCostUsd` a string.

`FleetJobOutcomeRecorder.onTerminal(job: FleetJobRecord): Promise<void>`: Target: same signature. First it records `fleet_fix_follow_up` for a qualifying `FIX` (call 1), whatever the requester type. Then it runs the baseline unchanged.

**Scope** — In: create the pure event module and colocated tests; extend job-outcome.recorder.ts and job-outcome.recorder.spec.ts while preserving all existing notification and ingest-correction behavior. The default existing test fixture has no FIX command, so assertions that outbox.record is not called remain unchanged. Out: US-002 subscriber/system key/module wiring, US-003 requester/repo skips, US-004 dispatch failures, US-005 real-database integration. A follow-up after a `FIX` whose outcome is `nothing`, including `nothing; pushed advisor ledger <sha>`: no code changed, so no review is queued. A follow-up after a `FIX` that ends `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`, `ESCALATED` or `CRASHED`. Logging or auditing a `FIX` that ends `COMPLETED` with `fixOutcome` `pushed` but no `resultSha` (the runner sets `resultSha` only when the pushed sha resolves): no event is recorded and nothing else happens.

**Interface** — `FIX_FOLLOW_UP = 'fleet_fix_follow_up'`; `buildFixFollowUpPayload(job: FleetJobRecord, prNumber: number, headSha: string): FixFollowUpPayload`; `parseFixFollowUpPayload(raw: unknown): FixFollowUpPayload | null`; `FleetJobOutcomeRecorder.onTerminal(job: FleetJobRecord): Promise<void>`. `FixFollowUpPayload` contains exactly the call 2 snapshot fields; identifiers/headSha/maxCostUsd are strings, leaseEpoch is a number, prNumber is a positive safe integer, requestedByType is USER | AGENT and profiles is string[].
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] When FleetJobOutcomeRecorder.onTerminal receives a FIX job in COMPLETED with fixOutcome 'pushed', resultSha 'a'.repeat(40) and feature 'review-pr-22', then it calls outbox.record with type 'fleet_fix_follow_up'.

[unit] When that qualifying FIX is recorded, then the event payload deep-equals { jobId, leaseEpoch, projectId, repoId, prNumber: 22, headSha: 'a'.repeat(40), requestedById, requestedByType, profiles, maxCostUsd }, with each value taken from the job.
[unit] When that qualifying FIX is recorded, then metadata deep-equals { projectId: <job projectId>, eventId: '<job id>:<leaseEpoch>:fix-follow-up' }.
[unit] When the same qualifying FIX has requestedByType 'AGENT', then it records a fleet_fix_follow_up payload whose requestedByType is 'AGENT'.
[unit] When a qualifying FIX record has no requestedByType, then it records a fleet_fix_follow_up payload whose requestedByType is 'USER'.

[unit] When onTerminal receives each table-driven case of a COMPLETED FIX with fixOutcome 'nothing', a FAILED FIX with fixOutcome 'pushed', a COMPLETED REVIEW, a qualifying FIX with resultSha null, or a qualifying FIX with feature 'review-pr-x', then it records no fleet_fix_follow_up event.
[unit] When parseFixFollowUpPayload receives the object returned by buildFixFollowUpPayload, then it returns a value deep-equal to its input.

[unit] When parseFixFollowUpPayload receives a valid payload altered in each table-driven case to requestedByType 'SYSTEM', prNumber 0, profiles [1], maxCostUsd the number 1, or jobId missing, then it returns null.

[unit] Given the existing recorder fixture with no FIX command and a USER requester, when onTerminal receives table-driven pairs (ESCALATED, null, escalated), (FAILED, null, failed), (CRASHED, null, crashed) or (COMPLETED, 'https://github.com/acme/app/pull/4', pr_opened), then outbox.record receives { type: 'fleet_job_outcome', payload: { jobId: 'j1', leaseEpoch: 2, projectId: 'p1', requestedById: 'u1', outcome: <row outcome>, repo: 'acme/app', feature: 'add', resultPrUrl: <row PR URL> }, metadata: { projectId: 'p1', eventId: 'j1:2' } }, preserving the existing notification payload and event id unchanged.

[unit] Given the existing fixture with no FIX command and no PR URL, when onTerminal receives CANCELLED, COMPLETED or RUNNING in each table-driven case, then outbox.record is not called, preserving the existing negative assertions.

[unit] When onTerminal receives a qualifying pushed FIX requested by an AGENT, then it records no fleet_job_outcome notification, preserving the existing agent-requester early return after recording the new follow-up event.

routing.reasoning: Add a pure event contract and a guarded enqueue to an existing transactional recorder; no new dependencies, authorization rules or persistence model.

modifiedFiles.reason: `onTerminal` gains the follow-up step before its existing agent-requester and thread-kind early return; the rest of the method is unchanged.

gains tests for the follow-up step; its existing assertions keep holding because the default job fixture has no `FIX` command, so `outbox.record` is still not called for the cases that assert it is not.

userStories.title: API fix follow-up subscriber, system key and dispatch
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Register the system writer and outbox subscriber that claims a pushed head, dispatches its REVIEW and links it to the FIX through audit.

**Motivation** — koda re-reviews the pushed head with decisions as a normal `REVIEW` job, which marks fixed threads and feeds K2 review memory.

**Approach** — 3. **One subscriber, one new system key.** `FixFollowUpSubscriber` (`apps/api/src/fleet/reviews/`) is `@SystemWriter('system.pr-fix.follow-up')`. It registers its handler for `fleet_fix_follow_up` on `FanOutPublisher` in `onModuleInit`, the pattern of `FleetJobOutcomeSubscriber`. The handler runs its body in `runAsSystem('pr-fix', fn, { onBehalfOf: { type: requestedByType, id: requestedById } })`. The component id is the key's second segment, so `SYSTEM_ACTOR_IDS` picks it up from the catalog unchanged.

5. **The head claim settles the poller race.** Before dispatching, the handler calls `insertPending(repoId, prNumber, headSha)` under `bookkeeping('fleet.pr-review-bookkeeping', ...)`. A `null` claim means the auto-review poller (or an earlier delivery of this event) already claimed that head. The handler then skips with reason `head_already_claimed`, and the poller's review covers the head. A successful dispatch calls `markDispatched(claim.id, reviewJob.id)`. The poller's `headIsOpen` then treats the head as settled. The handler never reopens a `pending` claim; only the poller's existing stale-claim recovery does, and only for repos with auto-review on.

6. **The dispatch.** `FleetJobsService.dispatch(requestedById, projectId, { command: 'REVIEW', repoId, prNumber, profiles, maxCostUsd: Number(maxCostUsd) }, { auditKey: 'system.pr-fix.follow-up' })`, with no transaction open. The `auditKey` union gains `'system.pr-fix.follow-up'`. Decisions are selected inside `dispatch` as for every `REVIEW` (K2), so the follow-up carries them. A follow-up `REVIEW` never queues anything itself: only a `FIX` records the event, so there is one round.

8. **One audit entry per handled event, on the FIX job.** `AuditRecorder.record({ key: 'system.pr-fix.follow-up', resourceType: 'fleet-job', resourceId: <FIX job id>, projectId, summary })` runs inside `txManager.run(() => audit.record(entry))`, with `TRANSACTION_MANAGER` injected, as `AuditRecorder.record` requires (`AuditRecorder.audited` is not used). The summary is `follow-up review dispatched: <review job id>` or `follow-up review skipped: <reason>`. A successful dispatch also has the job's own dispatch audit (key `system.pr-fix.follow-up`, actor `SYSTEM/pr-fix`, on behalf of the requester); the entry on the FIX job is the link between the two jobs.

9. **The handler throws only on database failure**, the `FleetJobOutcomeSubscriber` rule. A malformed payload logs a warning and returns. A throw from the requester reads (`findPrincipalAccess`, `effectiveKeys`), the repo read, a claim, a mark, a removal or an audit write makes the relay redeliver. When the claim still exists (after a dispatch or a `markFailed`), the redelivery finds the head already claimed and skips with `head_already_claimed` instead of dispatching twice. When the claim was removed (`budget_paused`, `review_active`, `dispatch_error`) and the audit write then failed, the redelivery claims again and retries the dispatch, which is safe because the first dispatch created no job. A database error thrown inside `FleetJobsService.dispatch` is not a handler throw: call 7's catch-all turns it into a final `dispatch_error` skip, as `ReviewHeadDispatcher` does.

10. **Head equality is not checked.** The follow-up reviews the PR's current head, which is whatever `nax bot review <pr>` sees when it runs. The claim names the head the FIX pushed. If someone pushes after the fix, the poller (when auto-review is on) reviews that newer head under its own claim.

**Scope** — In: parsing, successful claim/dispatch/mark/audit, fixed constructor, FanOutPublisher seam, new system key and writer registration, and unit-level DI compilation. US-003 implements requester/repo checks and audited skip paths; US-004 implements dispatch failure mapping; the full call 5/9 contracts above describe the final boundary and must not motivate extra work outside this story. US-002 fixtures already stub a granted requester (findPrincipalAccess returns an existing, enabled principal; effectiveKeys includes fleet.job.dispatch) and existing repo (findReviewRepo returns it), so US-003 does not replace fixtures. Out: US-001 event production, US-003 access/repo/claimed-head skip behavior, US-004 error outcomes, US-005 database flow. A second fix round, or a follow-up queued by a follow-up `REVIEW`: only a `FIX` records the event. Checking that the PR's current head still equals the pushed sha before dispatching: the follow-up reviews whatever head the PR has when the review runs. Web, CLI or notification display of the follow-up link: it lives in the audit log only.

Modify apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/fleet-jobs.service.ts only to extend dispatch opts.auditKey. Preserve the default-key regression in apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/fleet-jobs.service.spec.ts:137-143: dispatch without opts.auditKey still records fleet.job.dispatch. Do not change default dispatch behavior. Add 'system.pr-fix.follow-up': ['system'] immediately after system.pr-review.dispatch in apps/api/src/permissions/catalog.ts. Add the matching system row to docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-permission-action-inventory.tsv immediately after the FleetPrReviewPass row, mirroring its columns but naming FixFollowUpSubscriber (outbox fleet_fix_follow_up), new key, system scope and subscriber source. Add FixFollowUpSubscriber after FleetPrReviewPass in system-writer.decorator.spec.ts and change the exact writer length from 36 to 37. Change the exact per-role cell count from 223 to 224 in role-matrix.spec.ts; in permissions/__snapshots__/role-matrix.json add only the new key after system.pr-review.dispatch for every role with ["non-role-key","non-role-key"], leaving all other entries identical. The key, writer class and module registration land together because the writer contract checks every system key against a booted writer. FleetReviewsModule imports OutboxModule and provides FixFollowUpSubscriber. Extend fleet-reviews.module.spec.ts with GlobalStubsModule to resolve the subscriber without a DB; preserve existing compilation tests with OutboxModule imported.

**Interface** — `FixFollowUpSubscriber` with `onModuleInit()` and `readonly handle: (payload: unknown) => Promise<void>`. Its constructor is fixed from the first story so later stories do not change it: `(registry: FanOutPublisher, @Inject(FLEET_PR_REVIEW_REPOSITORY) reviews: IFleetPrReviewRepository, jobs: FleetJobsService, repos: FleetReposService, permissions: PermissionService, audit: AuditRecorder, @Inject(TRANSACTION_MANAGER) txManager: ITransactionManager)`.

`FleetJobsService.dispatch` opts target: `auditKey?: 'fleet.job.dispatch' | 'thread.plan' | 'thread.run' | 'system.schedule.dispatch' | 'system.pr-review.dispatch' | 'system.pr-fix.follow-up'`. Behaviour is unchanged. `insertPending(repoId: string, prNumber: number, headSha: string): Promise<FleetPrReviewRecord | null>`; `markDispatched(id: string, jobId: string): Promise<void>`. Consume `FIX_FOLLOW_UP`, `buildFixFollowUpPayload(job: FleetJobRecord, prNumber: number, headSha: string): FixFollowUpPayload` and `parseFixFollowUpPayload(raw: unknown): FixFollowUpPayload | null` from US-001. FanOutPublisher.publish of a record built by that builder is the story's integration seam, with collaborators stubbed at unit level.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] When FixFollowUpSubscriber.onModuleInit runs, then FanOutPublisher.register is called with 'fleet_fix_follow_up' and the subscriber's handle.
[unit] When handle receives a payload rejected by parseFixFollowUpPayload, then it logs a warning.
[unit] When handle receives a payload rejected by parseFixFollowUpPayload, then FleetJobsService.dispatch is not called and no claim, job or audit entry is written.
[unit] When handle receives a valid payload whose requester is granted, then insertPending is called with the payload's repoId, prNumber and headSha.

[unit] When handle receives that valid payload, then FleetJobsService.dispatch is called with arguments deep-equal to (requestedById, projectId, { command: 'REVIEW', repoId, prNumber, profiles, maxCostUsd: Number(payload.maxCostUsd) }, { auditKey: 'system.pr-fix.follow-up' }), using the payload's values.
[unit] When that dispatch call executes, then its action context actor equals { type: 'SYSTEM', id: 'pr-fix' }.
[unit] When that dispatch call executes, then its action context onBehalfOf equals { type: <payload requestedByType>, id: <payload requestedById> }.
[unit] When dispatch resolves with job id 'rev-1', then markDispatched is called with the claim's id and 'rev-1'.

[unit] When that dispatch succeeds, then AuditRecorder.record is called inside txManager.run with { key: 'system.pr-fix.follow-up', resourceType: 'fleet-job', resourceId: <payload jobId>, projectId: <payload projectId>, summary: 'follow-up review dispatched: rev-1' }.

[unit] When FanOutPublisher.publish receives an outbox record of type 'fleet_fix_follow_up' with a buildFixFollowUpPayload payload, the subscriber registered and the requester granted, then exactly one FleetJobsService.dispatch call has DTO command 'REVIEW'.
[unit] When the class-to-key declarations from @SystemWriter are read, then FixFollowUpSubscriber maps to 'system.pr-fix.follow-up'.
[unit] When FleetReviewsModule is compiled with the global test stubs, then it resolves FixFollowUpSubscriber.
[unit] When insertPending rejects with a database error, then handle rejects.
[unit] When markDispatched rejects with a database error after successful dispatch, then handle rejects.
[unit] When the successful-dispatch audit write rejects with a database error, then handle rejects.

routing.reasoning: Cross-module event dispatch, actor/onBehalfOf attribution, catalog/inventory contracts and DI wiring; system permission registration invokes the security override.

modifiedFiles.reason: the `dispatch` opts `auditKey` union gains `'system.pr-fix.follow-up'`; no behaviour change.

the catalog spec re-derives the catalog from this file; it gains one system row for FixFollowUpSubscriber (outbox fleet_fix_follow_up) with key system.pr-fix.follow-up and catalog scope system, placed right after the FleetPrReviewPass row at line 261 and mirroring its columns.

the writers map (lines 41-79) gains FixFollowUpSubscriber with key system.pr-fix.follow-up placed after FleetPrReviewPass, and the length assertion (line 103) changes from 36 to 37; AC-5 then holds for the new system key.
the per-role cell count (line 224) changes from 223 to 224 for the new system key; it stays an exact count.
every role gains system.pr-fix.follow-up, placed right after system.pr-review.dispatch, as non-role-key, non-role-key, like system.pr-review.dispatch. Every other entry stays identical.

userStories.title: API fix follow-up skips
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Revalidate the requester and repo before claiming the pushed head, and audit access, missing-repo and claimed-head skips on the FIX job.

**Motivation** — nax's own post-push re-review cannot take koda's decisions, so it could raise again a finding the team already settled.

**Approach** — 4. **Requester re-check (the K1-B enabler rule).** The handler loads the requester's access with `FleetPrReviewRepository.findPrincipalAccess` and its keys with `PermissionService.effectiveKeys(requester, { projectId })`. It goes on only when `mayDispatch(access, keys)` holds. Otherwise it skips with reason `requester_lost_access`. Nothing is turned off, because there is no setting to turn off. Next it reads the repo with `FleetReposService.findReviewRepo(repoId)`. A `null` result skips with reason `repo_gone`, before any claim: `FleetPrReview.repoId` is a foreign key to `FleetRepo`, so a claim on a deleted repo would throw instead of returning `null`. A repo deleted between this read and the claim makes the claim throw; the relay redelivers, and the redelivery skips with `repo_gone`.

5. **The head claim settles the poller race.** Before dispatching, the handler calls `insertPending(repoId, prNumber, headSha)` under `bookkeeping('fleet.pr-review-bookkeeping', ...)`. A `null` claim means the auto-review poller (or an earlier delivery of this event) already claimed that head. The handler then skips with reason `head_already_claimed`, and the poller's review covers the head. A successful dispatch calls `markDispatched(claim.id, reviewJob.id)`. The poller's `headIsOpen` then treats the head as settled. The handler never reopens a `pending` claim; only the poller's existing stale-claim recovery does, and only for repos with auto-review on.

8. **One audit entry per handled event, on the FIX job.** `AuditRecorder.record({ key: 'system.pr-fix.follow-up', resourceType: 'fleet-job', resourceId: <FIX job id>, projectId, summary })` runs inside `txManager.run(() => audit.record(entry))`, with `TRANSACTION_MANAGER` injected, as `AuditRecorder.record` requires (`AuditRecorder.audited` is not used). The summary is `follow-up review dispatched: <review job id>` or `follow-up review skipped: <reason>`. A successful dispatch also has the job's own dispatch audit (key `system.pr-fix.follow-up`, actor `SYSTEM/pr-fix`, on behalf of the requester); the entry on the FIX job is the link between the two jobs.

9. **The handler throws only on database failure**, the `FleetJobOutcomeSubscriber` rule. A malformed payload logs a warning and returns. A throw from the requester reads (`findPrincipalAccess`, `effectiveKeys`), the repo read, a claim, a mark, a removal or an audit write makes the relay redeliver. When the claim still exists (after a dispatch or a `markFailed`), the redelivery finds the head already claimed and skips with `head_already_claimed` instead of dispatching twice. When the claim was removed (`budget_paused`, `review_active`, `dispatch_error`) and the audit write then failed, the redelivery claims again and retries the dispatch, which is safe because the first dispatch created no job. A database error thrown inside `FleetJobsService.dispatch` is not a handler throw: call 7's catch-all turns it into a final `dispatch_error` skip, as `ReviewHeadDispatcher` does.

**Scope** — In: extend the subscriber created in US-002, reuse its full constructor and already-granted fixtures, add fix-follow-up.subscriber.skips.spec.ts and extend success fixtures only as needed. Access checks use the original USER or AGENT principal and project-scoped effective keys; require exists && !disabled && keys.has('fleet.job.dispatch'). Each skip audit uses the new key, resourceType fleet-job, resourceId FIX jobId and payload projectId in its own txManager.run. Preserve US-002 success/actor behavior. Out: US-001 producer, US-002 catalog/registration work, US-004 dispatch error mapping and US-005 full database flow. Turning anything off when the requester has lost access: there is no stored setting for a follow-up. Recovering a follow-up whose handler stopped between the claim and `markDispatched` (a crash or a database failure): the `pending` claim makes every redelivery skip as `head_already_claimed`; only the K1-B poller's stale-claim recovery reopens it, and only when auto-review is on for the repo. When the stop came after a successful dispatch (`markDispatched` failed), that recovery dispatches a second `REVIEW` of an already-reviewed head.

**Interface** — `findPrincipalAccess(ref: PrincipalRef): Promise<PrincipalAccess>`; `mayDispatch(access, keys)`; `FleetReposService.findReviewRepo(id: string): Promise<Pick<FleetRepoRecord, 'id' | 'projectId' | 'owner' | 'name' | 'githubInstallationId'> | null>`; `insertPending(repoId: string, prNumber: number, headSha: string): Promise<FleetPrReviewRecord | null>`. Preserve `readonly handle: (payload: unknown) => Promise<void>` and constructor `(registry: FanOutPublisher, @Inject(FLEET_PR_REVIEW_REPOSITORY) reviews: IFleetPrReviewRepository, jobs: FleetJobsService, repos: FleetReposService, permissions: PermissionService, audit: AuditRecorder, @Inject(TRANSACTION_MANAGER) txManager: ITransactionManager)`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] When mayDispatch is false because the requester's effective keys lack 'fleet.job.dispatch', then handle does not call insertPending.
[unit] When that requester lacks dispatch access, then AuditRecorder.record is called with summary 'follow-up review skipped: requester_lost_access' and resourceId equal to the payload's jobId.
[unit] When the requester's access is disabled although its keys include 'fleet.job.dispatch', then handle does not call insertPending.
[unit] When FleetReposService.findReviewRepo returns null for the payload's repoId, then handle does not call insertPending.
[unit] When that repo read returns null, then AuditRecorder.record is called with summary 'follow-up review skipped: repo_gone'.
[unit] When insertPending returns null, then handle does not call dispatch.
[unit] When insertPending returns null, then AuditRecorder.record is called with summary 'follow-up review skipped: head_already_claimed'.
[unit] When AuditRecorder.record rejects with a database error after a head_already_claimed skip, then handle rejects.
[unit] When findPrincipalAccess reports that the requester is gone, then handle performs no claim or dispatch.
[unit] When findPrincipalAccess reports that the requester is gone, then the FIX job's audit summary is 'follow-up review skipped: requester_lost_access'.
[unit] When findPrincipalAccess, effectiveKeys or findReviewRepo rejects with a database error in each table-driven case, then handle rejects.
[unit] When a repo deletion between findReviewRepo and insertPending causes the claim to reject with a database error, then handle rejects.
[unit] When a requester_lost_access or repo_gone skip's audit write rejects with a database error in each table-driven case, then handle rejects.

[unit] When the requester is disabled although its keys include 'fleet.job.dispatch', then AuditRecorder.record receives summary 'follow-up review skipped: requester_lost_access' on the payload's FIX jobId.

routing.reasoning: Reuse established requester/repo gates and audited skip patterns; requester permission and disabled-principal enforcement require strict security-isolated TDD.

userStories.title: API fix follow-up dispatch failures
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Map dispatch refusals and unexpected errors to the specified head-claim cleanup and FIX audit outcomes without swallowing persistence failures outside dispatch.

**Motivation** — koda re-reviews the pushed head with decisions as a normal `REVIEW` job, which marks fixed threads and feeds K2 review memory.

**Approach** — 7. **Dispatch failures mirror `ReviewHeadDispatcher`.** The checks run in this order, because `BudgetPausedException` extends `ConflictAppException`:
- `BudgetPausedException`: remove the claim, reason `budget_paused`.
- `ConflictAppException` with response prefix `fleet.jobs`: remove the claim, reason `review_active`.
- `ValidationAppException`, `NotFoundAppException` or `FleetDispatchException`: `markFailed(claim.id, 'failed:<reason>')` (cut to 200 characters), reason `<reason>`. `<reason>` is the validation response's `args.reason` when it is a string, else the exception's class name.
- Any other error: remove the claim, log a warning naming the FIX job id and the error class, reason `dispatch_error`.

8. **One audit entry per handled event, on the FIX job.** `AuditRecorder.record({ key: 'system.pr-fix.follow-up', resourceType: 'fleet-job', resourceId: <FIX job id>, projectId, summary })` runs inside `txManager.run(() => audit.record(entry))`, with `TRANSACTION_MANAGER` injected, as `AuditRecorder.record` requires (`AuditRecorder.audited` is not used). The summary is `follow-up review dispatched: <review job id>` or `follow-up review skipped: <reason>`. A successful dispatch also has the job's own dispatch audit (key `system.pr-fix.follow-up`, actor `SYSTEM/pr-fix`, on behalf of the requester); the entry on the FIX job is the link between the two jobs.

9. **The handler throws only on database failure**, the `FleetJobOutcomeSubscriber` rule. A malformed payload logs a warning and returns. A throw from the requester reads (`findPrincipalAccess`, `effectiveKeys`), the repo read, a claim, a mark, a removal or an audit write makes the relay redeliver. When the claim still exists (after a dispatch or a `markFailed`), the redelivery finds the head already claimed and skips with `head_already_claimed` instead of dispatching twice. When the claim was removed (`budget_paused`, `review_active`, `dispatch_error`) and the audit write then failed, the redelivery claims again and retries the dispatch, which is safe because the first dispatch created no job. A database error thrown inside `FleetJobsService.dispatch` is not a handler throw: call 7's catch-all turns it into a final `dispatch_error` skip, as `ReviewHeadDispatcher` does.

**Scope** — In: extend the US-002 subscriber, preserve its constructor and US-003 gates, add fix-follow-up.subscriber.outcomes.spec.ts with the existing fixture pattern, and apply bookkeeping('fleet.pr-review-bookkeeping', ...) to every removal or failure mark. Keep try/catch limited to jobs.dispatch so claim/mark/remove/audit database failures escape; markDispatched remains outside this dispatch-error catch. Audit failures escape even after cleanup. The audit reason is not truncated to the claim-outcome limit; markFailed gets `failed:${reason}` sliced to 200 characters. Out: producer (US-001), key/wiring/success flow (US-002), pre-dispatch skips (US-003), and real-DB proof (US-005). Retrying a skipped follow-up later (for example after a budget pause lifts or an active review ends): a skip is final, and auto-review covers the head when it is enabled for the repo. Redelivering after a database error thrown inside `FleetJobsService.dispatch`: it is a final `dispatch_error` skip, as in `ReviewHeadDispatcher`. A skip audited as `dispatch_error` although `FleetJobsService.dispatch` created the `REVIEW` row before it threw (for example from placement): this mirrors `ReviewHeadDispatcher`, and the queued `REVIEW` still runs. Changing the K1-B poller, `ReviewHeadDispatcher` or the `fleet.pr-review-bookkeeping` reason text; that text names `system.pr-review.dispatch` and is reused unchanged for the follow-up's claims.

**Interface** — `markFailed(id: string, outcome: string): Promise<void>`; `remove(id: string): Promise<void>`; preserve `readonly handle: (payload: unknown) => Promise<void>` and constructor `(registry: FanOutPublisher, @Inject(FLEET_PR_REVIEW_REPOSITORY) reviews: IFleetPrReviewRepository, jobs: FleetJobsService, repos: FleetReposService, permissions: PermissionService, audit: AuditRecorder, @Inject(TRANSACTION_MANAGER) txManager: ITransactionManager)`. Use `BudgetPausedException`, `ConflictAppException`, `ValidationAppException`, `NotFoundAppException`, `FleetDispatchException`, as imported by `apps/api/src/fleet/reviews/review-head-dispatcher.ts:1-6`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] When dispatch rejects in table-driven cases, then { removed: <ids passed to remove>, summary: <audit summary> } deep-equals BudgetPausedException -> { removed: [claim.id], summary: 'follow-up review skipped: budget_paused' }; ConflictAppException with response prefix 'fleet.jobs' -> { removed: [claim.id], summary: 'follow-up review skipped: review_active' }; plain Error -> { removed: [claim.id], summary: 'follow-up review skipped: dispatch_error' }.

[unit] When dispatch rejects in table-driven cases, then { failed: <markFailed arguments>, summary: <audit summary> } deep-equals ValidationAppException with args.reason 'review is GitHub-only' -> { failed: [claim.id, 'failed:review is GitHub-only'], summary: 'follow-up review skipped: review is GitHub-only' }; NotFoundAppException -> { failed: [claim.id, 'failed:NotFoundAppException'], summary: 'follow-up review skipped: NotFoundAppException' }; FleetDispatchException -> { failed: [claim.id, 'failed:FleetDispatchException'], summary: 'follow-up review skipped: FleetDispatchException' }.
[unit] When dispatch rejects with BudgetPausedException, then handle does not call markFailed.
[unit] When dispatch rejects with ValidationAppException whose args.reason is 300 characters long, then markFailed receives an outcome of exactly 200 characters starting with 'failed:'.
[unit] When dispatch rejects with a plain Error, then handle logs one warning whose text contains the payload's jobId and the error's class name.
[unit] When dispatch rejects with a plain Error, then handle resolves.
[unit] When dispatch rejects with BudgetPausedException and the following remove rejects with a database error, then handle rejects.
[unit] When markFailed rejects with a database error after a permanent dispatch refusal, then handle rejects.
[unit] When remove rejects with a database error after review_active or dispatch_error in each table-driven case, then handle rejects.
[unit] When an audit write rejects with a database error after dispatch-error cleanup or failure marking, then handle rejects.
[unit] When a database error originates inside FleetJobsService.dispatch and claim removal and audit succeed, then handle resolves with FIX audit summary 'follow-up review skipped: dispatch_error'.

routing.reasoning: Localized failure mapping mirrors an existing dispatcher; exception ordering and catch boundaries are important but introduce no new authorization or abstractions.

userStories.title: API fix follow-up end-to-end flow
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the binding real-database integration scenario proving that a runner-reported pushed FIX produces one follow-up REVIEW, settled head claim and linked FIX audit.

**Motivation** — Live check §9.155 (sandbox PR #22) showed the fix commit landing with no follow-up review.

**Approach** — Adds an integration test from a `FIX` terminal report on the runner sync path through `FanOutPublisher.publish` to the follow-up `REVIEW` row, its head claim and its audit entry, on the real test database.

The outermost entry point for the whole flow is the runner sync report (`JobReportProcessor`) applying a `FIX`'s snapshot and its `COMPLETED` state. US-005's integration AC enters there and ends at the follow-up `REVIEW` row.

A running FIX reports a snapshot carrying fixOutcome 'pushed' and resultSha, then UPLOADING then COMPLETED through the actual runner sync path. After that transaction commits, locate the real fleet_fix_follow_up outbox row and deliver it with FanOutPublisher.publish. Use the existing seeded HTTP runner world and enabled requester with fleet.job.dispatch, an existing GitHub repo, real service dispatch, real head repository and real audit persistence. Assert REVIEW uses feature review-pr-<n>, FIX profiles, cost cap and requester; the shared head row is dispatched and linked to the new job, and the FIX audit links the REVIEW id. Publish the same row again to assert no second REVIEW and the head_already_claimed audit. Do not replace terminal report processing with onTerminal calls, fabricate the event under test or mock away persisted outputs.

**Scope** — In: create only apps/api/test/integration/fleet/fleet-fix-follow-up.integration.spec.ts, using repository, runner lifecycle and FIX-snapshot fixture patterns. This explicitly binding test-only story remains separate despite generic story guidance. Use canRunDbTests, fixtureDb/action-context helpers, resetDb and bootHttpApp. Run bun run test:scoped test/integration/fleet/fleet-fix-follow-up.integration.spec.ts outside the sandbox on real test Postgres; KODA_DB_TESTS=1 is required, and a sandbox skip is not verification. Avoid concurrent force-reset DB runs; a second checkout uses KODA_TEST_DB_CONTAINER=1. Out: any production changes from US-001 through US-004, new UI/CLI/notification surfaces, extra recovery or a second fix round.

**Interface** — `FanOutPublisher.register(type, handler)`; `publish(record)` runs each handler in `runAsSystem('outbox')` and throws one aggregate error when any handler throws. Exercise the registered `FixFollowUpSubscriber` with `readonly handle: (payload: unknown) => Promise<void>` indirectly through publish of the committed outbox row. `FleetPrReview` is uniquely keyed by (repoId, prNumber, headSha); the expected outcome is dispatched and jobId is the REVIEW id. No production interface is added or changed in this story.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] Given the real test database and a running FIX job, when the runner sync path reports, in sequence, a snapshot carrying fixOutcome 'pushed' and a resultSha, state UPLOADING and state COMPLETED, and FanOutPublisher.publish delivers the fleet_fix_follow_up outbox row that report left after commit, then exactly one REVIEW job is created for the same repo with feature 'review-pr-<n>'.
[integration] When that follow-up REVIEW is created, then its profiles, maxCostUsd and requestedById equal the FIX job's.
[integration] When that flow completes, then FleetPrReview holds one row for (repoId, prNumber, resultSha) with outcome 'dispatched' and jobId equal to the new REVIEW job's id.
[integration] When that flow completes, then an audit entry exists with key 'system.pr-fix.follow-up', resourceId equal to the FIX job id and summary 'follow-up review dispatched: <REVIEW job id>'.
[integration] When the same persisted outbox row is published a second time, then no second REVIEW job is created.
[integration] When the same persisted outbox row is published a second time, then an audit entry is written with summary 'follow-up review skipped: head_already_claimed'.

routing.reasoning: One integration file reuses existing HTTP runner, FIX snapshot, database and fan-out fixtures after all production seams exist; standard persistence assertions and duplicate-delivery checks need no new abstractions or authorization changes.

analysis:
Repository examination and authority: This is an enhancement of the existing API, not greenfield work. The codebase-memory MCP tools are unavailable in this host, so discovery used direct Read/Grep tools. All five binding stories retain workdir apps/api and the exact linear dependency chain. API guidance is .nax/mono/apps/api/context.md:1-272. The supplied detected Express/Next.js labels are inaccurate: the API guidance specifies NestJS 12 + Fastify, Prisma 7 and Vitest (.nax/mono/apps/api/context.md:24-36); web is Nuxt and is untouched. Implementers must follow the nathapp-nestjs-patterns skill before writing NestJS code; no matching skill file was exposed by repository discovery. No implementation or tests were run during PRD authoring.

Goal and completion: A COMPLETED FIX with fixOutcome pushed, a resultSha and a parseable review-pr-N feature records an attempt-specific fleet_fix_follow_up event atomically with its terminal transition. After commit a system/pr-fix subscriber revalidates the original USER or AGENT, checks repo existence, competes for the existing head claim, dispatches one ordinary REVIEW with the FIX snapshot's profiles and cost cap, marks the claim, and audits the outcome on the FIX. Existing REVIEW decision selection supplies K2 memory without new decision logic. Completion includes a real-Postgres runner-sync-to-outbox-to-REVIEW integration scenario and a redelivery assertion, not just isolated subscriber tests.

US-001 producer and event seam: apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/job-outcome.recorder.ts:22-31 has a two-argument constructor and immediately returns for agent requesters or thread kinds. Insert the qualifying FIX enqueue BEFORE that return, retaining the constructor and existing notification behavior. Its existing enqueue records fleet_job_outcome with metadata eventId jobId:leaseEpoch (job-outcome.recorder.ts:41-49); the follow-up must use the distinct jobId:leaseEpoch:fix-follow-up suffix and payload builder. Existing recorder tests use a minimal fixture without command, so their negative outbox assertions remain valid (job-outcome.recorder.spec.ts:4-34). The pure notification builder/parser pattern is apps/api/src/notifications/fleet/fleet-notification-events.ts:37-47,59-71. FleetJobRecord already exposes profiles, decimal-as-string maxCostUsd, optional USER/AGENT requestedByType, resultSha and optional fixOutcome (apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/domain/fleet-job.domain.ts:65-133); no schema change is needed. Reuse prNumberOfReviewFeature, whose anchored regex and safe positive integer checks are at apps/api/src/fleet/common/review-jobs.ts:7-12. JobTransitionsService.apply updates first and calls outcomes.onTerminal(after) for terminal jobs inside the caller's transaction (apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/job-transitions.service.ts:29-31,61-69). JobReportProcessor.process owns txManager.run, mirrors snapshots in event sequence and applies runner state changes through transitions (apps/api/src/fleet/sync/job-report.processor.ts:68-70,97-138). Thus the recorder must only record, never dispatch. Other dependencies: FleetJobsModule provides/exports the recorder (apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/fleet-jobs.module.ts:18,35,42), and BundleIngestService injects it for existing correction behavior (apps/api/src/fleet/ingest/bundle-ingest.service.ts:22,47). Keep onIngestCorrection unchanged and do not add notifications-module imports to fleet modules.

US-002 subscriber, wiring and attribution: apps/api/src/notifications/fleet/fleet-job-outcome.subscriber.ts:12-35 demonstrates @SystemWriter, onModuleInit registration, a stable readonly arrow handle and malformed-payload warning. FanOutPublisher.register deduplicates the same handler; publish runs each handler in runAsSystem('outbox'), aggregates failures and triggers relay retries (apps/api/src/outbox/fan-out-publisher.ts:53-91). The new subscriber must enter its own runAsSystem('pr-fix', ..., {onBehalfOf}) so dispatch and FIX audit attribution are SYSTEM/pr-fix, not SYSTEM/outbox. runAsSystem validates component ids and opens an audit scope (apps/api/src/action-context/action-context.ts:130-146); actorTypeFor derives AGENT attribution from onBehalfOf (same file:175-186). The new catalog key makes pr-fix a recognized system actor through the existing catalog-derived ids; do not hardcode a new actor registry. FleetJobsService.dispatch currently allows five audit keys (apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/fleet-jobs.service.ts:79); add only the new union member. Dispatch validates the repo/provider, budgets and normalized input, selects decisions before its insert transaction, writes its own audit inside that transaction, translates duplicate-active insertion after rollback, then publishes/places (same file:80-174). Do not wrap dispatch in an outer transaction and do not reimplement REVIEW decisions.

The writer key, class and module registration must land together: INVENTORY_SCOPE_ROWS currently places system.pr-review.dispatch at apps/api/src/permissions/catalog.ts:345. Add system.pr-fix.follow-up immediately after it. The catalog spec reconstructs entries from the root TSV (apps/api/src/permissions/catalog.spec.ts:16-30,111-120), so docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-permission-action-inventory.tsv:261 also needs a system row for FixFollowUpSubscriber (outbox fleet_fix_follow_up), mirroring FleetPrReviewPass columns. This is the only root-scoped file change, but the binding workdir remains apps/api. The writer map currently lists FleetPrReviewPass at apps/api/src/permissions/system-writer.decorator.spec.ts:52 and asserts length 36 at :103; add the new class/key after that writer and change 36 to 37, preserving exact contract checks. apps/api/src/permissions/role-matrix.spec.ts:220-224 currently asserts 11 rows with 223 cells each: retain exact counts, changing cells to 224. Each role in apps/api/src/permissions/__snapshots__/role-matrix.json gains only system.pr-fix.follow-up immediately after system.pr-review.dispatch with [non-role-key, non-role-key]; all other entries remain identical. FleetReviewsModule already imports repo/jobs/git-broker/memory modules and binds the private review repository (apps/api/src/fleet/reviews/fleet-reviews.module.ts:25-40); import OutboxModule and provide the subscriber without changing exports unnecessarily. OutboxModule exports OutboxCoreModule and requires configured outbox options (apps/api/src/outbox/outbox.module.ts:16-35). Extend the existing no-DB GlobalStubsModule compile tests at apps/api/src/fleet/reviews/fleet-reviews.module.spec.ts:29-84, not an integration DI test. US-002 takes the full fixed constructor now, with granted-requester and existing-repo stubs ready for US-003.

US-003 access and claim concurrency: Reuse the USER/AGENT PrincipalRef lookup pattern in apps/api/src/fleet/reviews/enabler-gate.ts:21-27 and mayDispatch in apps/api/src/fleet/schedules/schedule-access.ts:12-14 (exists, not disabled, effective fleet.job.dispatch key). Unlike EnablerGate.check, do not call disableAutoReview: the follow-up has no stored setting. Check permission before repo before claim. FleetReposService.findReviewRepo returns a minimal repo or null at apps/api/src/fleet/repos/fleet-repos.service.ts:109-114. FleetPrReview has a cascading repo FK and unique (repoId,prNumber,headSha) at apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:800-813. Reading a deleted repo before claiming avoids an FK failure; deletion after the read is a database failure to propagate so redelivery can observe repo_gone. IFleetPrReviewRepository defines the entire reusable seam at apps/api/src/fleet/reviews/domain/fleet-pr-review.domain.ts:29-40. PrismaFleetPrReviewRepository.insertPending returns null only for P2002 and rethrows other failures; mutations and principal reads are at apps/api/src/fleet/reviews/prisma-fleet-pr-review.repository.ts:49-83. Place head insert/mark/remove operations inside the existing bookkeeping reason. ReviewHeadDispatcher's stale-pending recovery is at apps/api/src/fleet/reviews/review-head-dispatcher.ts:82-91: the follow-up must not copy that recovery. If poller or another delivery won the same head, audit head_already_claimed and dispatch nothing.

US-004 failure semantics and transaction boundaries: Mirror apps/api/src/fleet/reviews/review-head-dispatcher.ts:98-150, checking BudgetPausedException before the broader ConflictAppException. Budget pause, fleet.jobs conflict and catch-all dispatch errors remove the claim; permanent dispatch refusals mark failed:<reason> truncated to 200 characters. Only ValidationAppException's string args.reason overrides the class-name reason. Keep the try/catch narrowly around jobs.dispatch: failures from access reads, repo reads, insertPending, markDispatched, markFailed, remove or audit must propagate rather than become dispatch_error. A database exception originating INSIDE jobs.dispatch is deliberately caught as dispatch_error. Catch-all warnings name the FIX job id and error class without logging untrusted payloads or secrets. AuditRecorder.record rejects outside a transaction and unknown keys (apps/api/src/audit/audit-recorder.service.ts:44-49), so each normal valid-event outcome writes the FIX entry through txManager.run(() => audit.record(entry)); do not use audited and do not hold that transaction across dispatch. The existing disableAutoReview implementation shows explicit txManager.run with record (apps/api/src/fleet/repos/fleet-repos.service.ts:129-139). Reuse the existing fleet.pr-review-bookkeeping reason unchanged, even though its text names the old writer (apps/api/src/action-context/audit-coverage.reasons.ts:20).

Retry and backward-compatibility risks: The shared unique head claim prevents ordinary double dispatch and settles the auto-review race without poller changes. This is not global exactly-once delivery or exactly-once auditing. A redelivery after a retained dispatched/failed/pending claim skips and writes a head_already_claimed audit, including when a previous audit failed. A crash after claiming can permanently suppress follow-up when auto-review is off; when on, existing stale-claim recovery can eventually reopen it and can duplicate a previously dispatched review if markDispatched failed. Removed-claim outcomes can retry if their audit failed, while successful skips are final. Catch-all dispatch failures may follow a committed job insertion/placement failure; the queued job can still run despite a dispatch_error skip. These are explicit non-goals, not defects to fix in this feature. The claim records the FIX's pushed sha, while the actual REVIEW sees whatever head nax finds; no new GitHub head/open-state check is permitted. Only FIX triggers an event, avoiding a recursive review/fix loop. Preserve normal fleet_job_outcome notifications alongside the additional event and avoid changing runner protocol, DTOs, decision selection, terminal workflow or enqueue-on-ingest behavior.

US-005 real-database flow: Keep this binding test-only story separate; it adds apps/api/test/integration/fleet/fleet-fix-follow-up.integration.spec.ts and no production code. Repository integration fixtures use canRunDbTests, resetDb, bootHttpApp, fixtureDb and actor-aware repository wrappers (apps/api/test/integration/fleet/fleet-pr-review.integration.spec.ts:1-56); they already prove unique head claims and repo cascade behavior (:64-99). Runner lifecycle fixtures show real authenticated sync with ASSIGN/ack/RUNNING and UPLOADING then COMPLETED (apps/api/test/integration/fleet/runner-sync-lifecycle.integration.spec.ts:33-48,107-118). A real FIX snapshot carrying fixOutcome and 40-hex resultSha is exercised at apps/api/test/integration/fleet/runner-sync.integration.spec.ts:250-275. Use those fixtures and enter through runner sync/JobReportProcessor, not a direct call to onTerminal or a fabricated follow-up payload; select the persisted outbox row after commit and publish it via FanOutPublisher. Configure a real enabled requester with dispatch permission and an existing GitHub repo, avoid uncontrolled background relay/poller races using the existing test harness configuration, and inspect the real REVIEW row, FleetPrReview row and audit storage. Publish the same persisted row again to prove no second REVIEW and the skip audit.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests are colocated *.spec.ts and use vi, not jest. Add pure event tests, extend recorder regression tests, add subscriber success/seam tests, separate skips and failure-mapping tests, and extend unit-level module compilation plus permission contract tests. Package scripts are apps/api/package.json:12-25: bun run test excludes integration/e2e; bun run test:scoped <files> is the targeted runner; integration runs require DB mode. US-002 and US-003 use strict three-session-tdd because they change system permission/access-control paths. Other stories use content-appropriate TDD routing. Run the US-005 scoped integration outside NAX_SANDBOXED=1 with KODA_DB_TESTS=1; sandbox skips do not verify DB behavior. The app guidance requires actual passing scoped DB execution for newly authored integration specs, uses isolated local test Postgres/Testcontainers, never inherited DATABASE_URL, and force-resets the test database; use KODA_TEST_DB_CONTAINER=1 for a parallel checkout (.nax/mono/apps/api/context.md:175-183). No schema migration, backfill, data conversion, public API change or OpenAPI/client regeneration is required: reuse FleetPrReview and generic project-scoped outbox storage. Existing completed FIX jobs are not retroactively scanned. Deploy the producer, consumer, key/inventory and module registration together after the ordered stories; no frontend, CLI, runner or notification display changes are part of this rollout.

Refine-pass adversarial audit: Re-read the persisted spec and rechecked recorder/recorder tests, ReviewHeadDispatcher error branches, dispatch service/default-key test, EnablerGate/mayDispatch, review domain/module/DI tests, fan-out publishing, runner FIX-snapshot fixture, HTTP app helper and global stubs. All 39 explicit spec ACs survive in their original stories. The following ordinal map enumerates every spec AC, using S for spec AC order within its story and D for the corresponding draft acceptanceCriteria position: US-001 S1 trigger->D1; S2 snapshot deep-equality with each value from the job->D2; S3 metadata->D3; S4 AGENT->D4; S5 absent type USER->D5; S6 all five non-trigger rows->D6; S7 builder/parser round-trip->D7; S8 all five malformed rows->D8. US-002 S1 register type and handle->D1; S2 malformed warning/no dispatch->D2,D3; S3 claim payload repo/PR/head->D4; S4 exact dispatch arguments from payload->D5; S5 SYSTEM/pr-fix actor->D6; S6 original requester onBehalfOf->D7; S7 markDispatched claim/rev-1->D8; S8 exact FIX audit inside txManager.run->D9; S9 builder-to-FanOutPublisher-to-one-REVIEW-dispatch seam with subscriber registered and requester granted->D10; S10 writer map->D11; S11 module resolves subscriber with global stubs->D12. US-003 S1 missing dispatch key/no claim->D1; S2 access skip summary and FIX resourceId->D2; S3 disabled despite key/no claim->D3; S4 null repo/no claim->D4; S5 repo_gone audit->D5; S6 null claim/no dispatch->D6; S7 head_already_claimed audit->D7; S8 database error from claimed-head skip audit rejects->D8. US-004 S1 all three claim-removal rows and their exact summary tuples->D1; S2 all three markFailed rows and their exact summary tuples->D2; S3 BudgetPausedException never markFailed->D3; S4 300-character reason produces 200-character failed: outcome->D4; S5 one warning names FIX id and error class->D5; S6 plain Error resolves->D6; S7 removal DB error after budget pause rejects->D7. US-005 S1 real-DB running FIX snapshot/UPLOADING/COMPLETED then publish actual outbox row produces one same-repo review-pr-N REVIEW->D1; S2 profiles/maxCostUsd/requestedById equality->D2; S3 unique pushed-head dispatched claim linked to REVIEW->D3; S4 exact FIX audit link->D4; S5 second publication creates no second REVIEW and writes head_already_claimed audit->D5,D6. No qualifying clauses were discarded; payload provenance, granted requester, registered subscriber, global stubs, actual persisted report row, same repo and same-event redelivery conditions remain attached to their assertions.

Failure-table audit: malformed warning/no writes/return is in US-002; missing/disabled/gone requester and missing repo are in US-003; duplicate head is in US-003 and US-005; budget pause, fleet.jobs conflict, each permanent refusal and catch-all dispatch error are in US-004; read/claim/mark/remove/audit persistence errors propagate in US-002 through US-004. Every story has negative-path ACs, including US-005 duplicate redelivery. Added explicit regression ACs for existing recorder payload/event id and negative assertions, suppression of agent notifications, dispatch's default audit key, pre-existing module providers, authorized USER/AGENT dispatch after gates, and success auditing after failure handling. The existing default-audit regression already exists at apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/fleet-jobs.service.spec.ts:137-143. The HTTP helper supports Fastify explicitly but defaults to AppFactory.create for current supertest fixtures (apps/api/test/helpers/http-app.ts:16-18,44-46); follow the existing integration fixtures rather than forcing a new adapter.

Context/scope/routing audit: Each contextFiles list exactly matches the spec's recommended list (five/five/five/three/five entries); only dependency-created files are future context, and each story's own new files remain solely in expectedFiles. All referenced dependencies exist and all four binding dependency edges remain unchanged. No descriptions contradict their ACs; broader verbatim final-design notes in US-002 are explicitly staged into US-003 and US-004 rather than excluded from the feature. All 15 feature-level Out of Scope bullets remain verbatim and in original order, with no story-local deferrals hoisted into that array. US-002 retains complex/three-session-tdd because its changes cross the permission catalog, system attribution, module registration and outbox/dispatch boundaries. US-003 retains medium/three-session-tdd for access enforcement. US-001 and US-004 remain medium/tdd-simple. US-005 is reduced to medium/tdd-simple because it adds one standard fixture-based integration file after the production seams exist, not a new integration architecture. No binding story was merged, split or renamed. These checks are a source-level PRD audit, not an assertion that implementation tests have run.
outOfScope: Dispatching `REVIEW` or `FIX` from the CLI, the assistant tool `koda_dispatch_job` or the web dispatch form, and a `Fix` action on a `REVIEW` job page; part B2 (`fleet-pr-fix-surfaces`).
A follow-up after a `FIX` whose outcome is `nothing`, including `nothing; pushed advisor ledger <sha>`: no code changed, so no review is queued.
A follow-up after a `FIX` that ends `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`, `ESCALATED` or `CRASHED`.
Checking that the PR's current head still equals the pushed sha before dispatching: the follow-up reviews whatever head the PR has when the review runs.
A second fix round, or a follow-up queued by a follow-up `REVIEW`: only a `FIX` records the event.
Retrying a skipped follow-up later (for example after a budget pause lifts or an active review ends): a skip is final, and auto-review covers the head when it is enabled for the repo.
A duplicate skip audit entry whenever the relay redelivers an event (after a database failure or a reclaimed delivery): the redelivery is audited as `head_already_claimed`.

Recovering a follow-up whose handler stopped between the claim and `markDispatched` (a crash or a database failure): the `pending` claim makes every redelivery skip as `head_already_claimed`; only the K1-B poller's stale-claim recovery reopens it, and only when auto-review is on for the repo. When the stop came after a successful dispatch (`markDispatched` failed), that recovery dispatches a second `REVIEW` of an already-reviewed head.
Redelivering after a database error thrown inside `FleetJobsService.dispatch`: it is a final `dispatch_error` skip, as in `ReviewHeadDispatcher`.

Logging or auditing a `FIX` that ends `COMPLETED` with `fixOutcome` `pushed` but no `resultSha` (the runner sets `resultSha` only when the pushed sha resolves): no event is recorded and nothing else happens.

A skip audited as `dispatch_error` although `FleetJobsService.dispatch` created the `REVIEW` row before it threw (for example from placement): this mirrors `ReviewHeadDispatcher`, and the queued `REVIEW` still runs.
Checking that the PR is still open: a `FIX` whose PR was closed or merged before the follow-up runs still queues the `REVIEW`, and that job fails with nax's reason.
Turning anything off when the requester has lost access: there is no stored setting for a follow-up.
Web, CLI or notification display of the follow-up link: it lives in the audit log only.
Changing the K1-B poller, `ReviewHeadDispatcher` or the `fleet.pr-review-bookkeeping` reason text; that text names `system.pr-review.dispatch` and is reused unchanged for the follow-up's claims.
